title: Reduce Venus sustained complete-frame CPU below the acceptance ceiling
description:
## Why

Orbit acceptance Bead orb-bi4.5.4 found one confirmed pre-graduation no-go at Orbit 847cab1ca37495c5cd45454623bd81909b488564 and Venus 8149002c7275a00db1c08fded171e09f249dd977. Release builds at a 929x976 window and authoritative 100x52 grid ran timeout 20s sh -c "while :; do seq 1 20000; done". Combined Orbit plus Venus CPU p95 was 240 percent, above the predeclared 200 percent ceiling. A same-shape attribution sample measured Orbit p95 101 percent and Venus p95 141 percent, making Venus the larger process-level cost. RSS and final convergence passed: 8.2 MiB growth and 116 ms after output quiesced.

Effort: M. Risk: MED. Confidence: HIGH that Venus owns the larger observed share; the internal limiting stage is not yet identified.

## Evidence

- src/model.rs:141-144 materializes every accepted protocol frame into a fresh Scene.
- src/scene.rs:104-146 clones the complete frame into Venus draw rows and cells.
- src/main.rs:113-170 applies every server message, refreshes accessibility and window state, and requests redraw.
- src/render.rs:302-408 prepares text, records a complete render pass, submits, and presents.
- src/render.rs:411-434 rebuilds all scene text and rectangles whenever the revision changes.
- orb-bi4.5.4 records exact revisions, environment, ceilings, workload, and process-level measurements.

## Scope

In scope:
- Venus-owned complete-frame materialization, scene rebuild, glyph preparation, and presentation costs.
- Private, bounded profiling sufficient to identify the dominant Venus stage.
- The smallest Venus-only correction that brings the accepted complete-frame path below the existing envelope.
- Preserve VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 and canonical ORBS v1.

Out of scope:
- Orbit code, tests, manifests, or ownership.
- A protocol revision, delta schema, dirty-row extraction, snapshot-plus-row-patch, public trace, alternate backend, or second terminal authority.
- History, ordered effects, graphics-resource expansion, remote transport, macOS support, or persistence.
- A direct crate unless a repository Crate gate selects it.

## Implementation Notes

1. Reproduce the exact release workload and segment Venus CPU among Scene::from_frame, refresh and accessibility, rebuild_if_needed, glyph preparation, submission, and presentation without changing the public boundary.
2. Identify the dominant measured stage before choosing code shape.
3. Apply the smallest Venus-owned correction and retain complete canonical frames plus snapshots as the resynchronization fallback.
4. Rerun the exact envelope and every canonical proof check for contracts touched.
5. If the measured cause requires an Orbit or protocol change, stop and report the compatibility decision instead of adding an adapter.

## Verification

- cargo fmt --check should exit 0.
- cargo check --locked should exit 0.
- cargo test --locked should exit 0.
- cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings should exit 0.
- The orb-bi4.5.4 sustained-output condition should report combined CPU p95 <= 200 percent, RSS <= 192 MiB, RSS growth <= 32 MiB, and final convergence <= 1 second.
- Shell, Neovim, Yazi, resize, and reattachment observations should preserve their accepted results.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the complete-frame flow has drifted materially from the cited revision.
- Stop if a correction requires changing ORBS v1, Orbit ownership, or another repository.
- Stop before adding a dependency, public instrumentation surface, dirty-row extraction, or patch protocol without the required gate and explicit user choice.
- Stop if the exact workload cannot reproduce the result; record the negative result rather than optimizing a guess.

## Maintenance Notes

This Bead hardens VEN-C1 and must preserve VEN-C2, VEN-C3, and VEN-C4. It consumes compatible ORB-C1 through ORB-C7 proofs through Orbit 847cab1. Complete frames remain accepted unless measured evidence and a separate user decision change the boundary.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The exact orb-bi4.5.4 release workload is reproducible and attributes the dominant Venus CPU stage with observed data.
2. A Venus-only correction brings combined Orbit plus Venus CPU p95 to <= 200 percent at 929x976 and 100x52 while RSS remains <= 192 MiB, growth <= 32 MiB, and final convergence <= 1 second.
3. VEN-C1 is hardened and VEN-C2 through VEN-C4 remain behaviorally preserved; canonical checks pass on the resulting exact revision.
4. ORBS v1, complete canonical frames, snapshot resynchronization, Orbit ownership, and the one-client boundary do not change.
5. No direct crate, public trace, dirty-row extraction, snapshot-plus-row-patch, adapter, or cross-repository change is introduced without its required gate and explicit user choice.
notes: Accepted state: Venus source proof 8929c9f9d151641a343813ddeb6005cb9c771286 and proof metadata cea6b00e122968fa5bd3f92ffb6b9d8bf54c2b4c harden VEN-C1 and preserve VEN-C2 through VEN-C4 against Orbit runtime 847cab1ca37495c5cd45454623bd81909b488564 and unchanged canonical protocol c905bf9610581747f1b07565814b501ca66cfaa6. Venus keeps one bounded native event queue. Complete frames are replaced across ordered Accepted acknowledgements only when the queued candidate is strictly newer than every previously delivered or queued frame and the incoming frame is strictly newer again; otherwise original order reaches FrameReducer, which remains the sole revision validator. Failures, invalid data, connection loss, and other semantic barriers retain ordering and first-cause behavior. ASCII uses basic shaping; non-ASCII retains advanced shaping. Exact Xwayland acceptance at 929x976 and 100x52 measured active combined CPU p95 167 percent, Orbit maximum 101 percent, Venus maximum 67 percent, peak combined RSS about 55.3 MiB, and 13.6 ms final convergence. Fifty fullscreen cycles returned coherently to 929x976 within 500 ms, and current state reattached in 122 ms while Orbit and its PTY survived client loss. Shell, Unicode, Neovim, and Yazi evidence remains preserved. Simplification retained one strong frame-reduction test for message barriers, delivered high-water, and non-increasing revisions. Container replacement, derived frame counting, notifier inlining, and batch refresh were rejected because they increased code or runtime work, moved rather than removed the concurrency concept, or risked observable accessibility/failure behavior. No protocol, dependency, public trace, Orbit, or cross-repository change was introduced. Platform disposition: isolated existing native-render dependency; no new macOS blocker. Material constraints remain: redraw cadence alone failed, a 33 ms scheduler remained above the ceiling, Accepted cannot be a coalescing barrier during resize storms, and reduction must never hide a revision failure.

title: Provide native history scrolling, selection, and copy
description:
Contract routing:
- Creates VEN-C7 when implementation is explicitly activated.
- Consumes ORB-C8 at `840a67c0cb32b334ed54888321d5ca77e58117b0` and ORB-C9 plus the breaking ORBS v2 replacement at `9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757`.
- Preserves VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 and keeps Orbit as the sole terminal, retained-history, viewport, selection, selected-presentation, and copied-text authority.
- Planning this Bead changes no product contract, protocol, manifest, or runtime behavior.

Goal:
Prove the minimum useful native-terminal interaction in Venus against the exact accepted Orbit owner. Venus captures native gestures, maps them to the last accepted complete frame, presents Orbit-authored selection, and performs the explicit native clipboard side effect. It does not cache or reconstruct terminal history.

Accepted compatibility order:
1. Orbit has proved ORBS v2 and ORB-C9 at `9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757`.
2. After Orbit `orb-j0m.5` closes, activate this Bead as the next single implementation frontier.
3. Update the exact `orbit-protocol` pin from the ORBS v1 consumer revision `c905bf9610581747f1b07565814b501ca66cfaa6` to the accepted Orbit proof.
4. Prove Venus, then let Orbit `orb-j0m.4` accept the real pair.

This is a breaking owner-to-consumer update. There is no ORBS v1 adapter, dual-version support, feature probe, compatibility window, second decoder, or handwritten schema.

Implementation shape:
- Wheel and trackpad input use the existing canonical semantic mouse message. Venus owns only bounded native scroll normalization: line deltas accumulate in line units, while pixel deltas normalize against the current rendered cell dimensions, and either source emits only whole semantic wheel steps. It keeps at most a sub-step remainder, drops non-finite input, caps emissions per native event, and clears residual state on focus loss, scale or geometry change, and reconnect. Orbit alone resolves authoritative application mouse tracking, DEC 1007 alternate scroll, primary-history viewport movement, clamping, no-op framing, and byte-producing-key return to live.
- Pointer gestures are mapped against the last accepted complete-frame revision and current viewport cells. Venus sends canonical ORBS v2 Begin, Update, Finish, and Copy actions in order.
- Orbit-authored complete frames remain the only source of cells, selected styling, cursor, title, and reconnect state. Venus keeps only transient native gesture state and the accepted frame required to render and hit-test it.
- Orbit returns exact bounded CopiedText only after an explicit Copy action. Venus writes that result to the native clipboard and never extracts terminal text from rendered cells.
- A non-selection terminal mutation cancels active selection. After Finish, terminal output, resize or reflow, and active-screen transitions clear selected presentation without changing the frozen copy candidate. A newer valid Begin, client loss, or exit clears it.
- Accessibility derives viewport and selection from the same accepted complete frame and reports interaction failures without inventing missing terminal state.

Explicit non-owners:
Venus has no history page cache, epoch, stable row anchor, row token, page request, gap repair, cache eviction, client-owned viewport, client-owned terminal selection content, or text reconstruction. Search, semantic command regions, richer word/line/rectangle selection, drag autoscroll, auto-copy, rich clipboard formats, terminal clipboard-write effects, restart persistence, tabs, panes, and workspace topology remain outside this Bead.

References before code:
- Required: exact Orbit ORB-C8/ORB-C9 proof and canonical ORBS v2 package; current Venus Scene, renderer, input, accessibility, lifecycle, and failure owners; exact winit and AccessKit surfaces already selected by the repository; and the repository's native clipboard path or a triggered native-platform decision.
- Comparison only: one mature native terminal interaction at an exact revision, limited to gesture precedence, accessibility, and clipboard UX.
- Rejected scope: client-side VT parsing, page caches, stable anchors, replay protocols, copied terminal implementations, and compatibility adapters.

Cheapest proof:
Use deterministic protocol-faithful tests against the exact canonical Orbit package for scroll-delta normalization, gesture-to-cell mapping, action ordering, stale revision rejection, authoritative selected frames, frozen copy behavior, mouse-mode precedence, reconnect, and bounded failure. Then dogfood the real Linux Orbit/Venus pair through shell history, rapid wheel movement, key return to live, wrapped Unicode and wide graphemes, forward and reverse selection, explicit copy, resize/reflow, alternate-screen Neovim and Yazi, mouse mode, DEC 1007, detach, reattach, client loss, oversized copy, and stopped-reader pressure.

Acceptance:
1. VEN-C7 and the exact ORB-C8/ORB-C9 proof revisions are indexed before implementation; the manifest pins the accepted ORBS v2 `orbit-protocol` revision.
2. Native wheel and trackpad deltas become a bounded count of canonical semantic wheel steps: fractional line movement accumulates in line units, sub-cell pixel movement accumulates against current cell dimensions, emission is capped, and residual state resets at native lifecycle boundaries. The resulting steps traverse Orbit-owned retained history and return to live without client history state or duplicate PTY bytes.
3. Application mouse reporting and DEC 1007 behavior remain Orbit-owned and take correct precedence over host scrolling.
4. Selection begins only against the exact last accepted complete-frame revision; stale revisions, invalid cells, invalid phase order, oversized work, and pressure fail deterministically without partial client state.
5. Venus renders authoritative selected styling from complete frames and never reparses or mirrors terminal text.
6. Explicit Copy places only Orbit-returned bounded CopiedText on the native clipboard. Output, resize/reflow, and screen transitions preserve the finished frozen candidate exactly as ORB-C9 specifies.
7. Resize/reflow, alternate-screen transitions, mutation cancellation, detach/reattach, client loss, and reconnect converge without a cache, stable-anchor, or second terminal owner.
8. Accessibility exposes the same accepted viewport, selected styling, copy success or failure, and reconnect state used visually.
9. Deterministic checks and real Linux dogfood cover the stated boundary; canonical locked Rust checks and git diff checking pass.
10. Closure records exact Orbit and Venus revisions, VEN-C and ORB-C IDs, breaking update order, commands, environment, bounds, latency, memory, queued output, dependency disposition, portability, LOC, and remaining limitations.
11. Orbit `orb-j0m.4` can accept the exact real pair for Eon dogfood without an adapter or client-side compensation.

Dependency decision:
No dependency is selected. Reuse the accepted Venus stack and native platform facilities. Any new crate or architecture-shaping native choice requires the repository gate and user approval.

Portability disposition:
Neutral gesture and protocol flow with clipboard and window-system effects isolated at existing platform seams. Linux is the proof target; macOS remains credible but unproved.

External gate:
This is the sole Venus consumer Bead for the pre-graduation native-interaction baseline. Keep it deferred until Orbit `orb-j0m.5` closes, then activate it as the next single implementation frontier. Orbit `orb-j0m.4` and Eon dogfood wait for the accepted VEN-C7 proof.

title: Activate safe native hyperlink interaction
description:
Contract routing:
- Creates VEN-C5 when implementation is explicitly activated.
- Consumes Orbit ORB-C6 and the exact accepted ORBF/ORBS proof revision current at activation.
- Preserves VEN-C1, VEN-C2, and VEN-C4. Planning this Bead changes no contract index or runtime behavior.

## Why

Orbit already emits explicit OSC 8 hyperlink URIs and Venus preserves each URI in its immutable scene, but Venus offers no native hyperlink action. Users therefore see linked text without a safe way to inspect, copy, or open the authoritative target.

## Evidence

- `src/scene.rs:42-48` stores the Orbit-authored hyperlink on each DrawCell.
- `src/scene.rs:285-297` materializes the URI directly from the canonical frame without reparsing terminal text.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:8-11` proves scene materialization and semantic input but indexes no hyperlink interaction.
- Orbit `docs/CONTRACTS.md:27` proves ORB-C6 and identifies rich presentation as an owned cross-repository boundary.

## Scope

In scope:
- Pointer hit testing against only the last successfully presented scene.
- Clear hover/focus affordance, target inspection, copy-link, and an explicit modifier-click or equivalent open action.
- A narrow scheme and length policy with bounded failure UX.
- Linux proof with a macOS-credible native-action seam.

Out of scope:
- Parsing URLs or file paths from ordinary terminal text.
- Silently opening a target, hiding the actual URI, or bypassing terminal mouse-reporting semantics.
- Workspace file navigation, custom schemes, shell integration, or any Orbit protocol/schema change unless a confirmed owner gap is reported back to Orbit.
design:
## Implementation Notes

1. Before code, add the user-approved VEN-C5 row to docs/CONTRACTS.md and record the exact consumed Orbit proof and compatibility classification.
2. Complete the Execution baseline and Reference gate. Required before code: the current OSC 8 specification or Ghostty VT documentation, the exact winit pointer/cursor APIs already selected, and official Linux/macOS external-open behavior. Compare only the native/standard-library path and credible opener crates if an opener dependency is actually needed.
3. Specify the interaction so terminal mouse reporting and selection retain priority; prefer an explicit modifier or context action rather than stealing ordinary clicks.
4. Derive link spans and hit targets from the accepted Scene. Do not add a second parser or mutable hyperlink model.
5. Apply URI size and scheme policy before invoking a native action. Opening and copying remain user-triggered.
6. Add one strong deterministic scene/hit/action-policy test and focused native dogfood.

Dependency decision: no crate is selected. A direct crate or architecture-shaping feature requires the Venus Crate gate and user approval before manifest edits.

Portability disposition: isolated platform dependency for external opening; scene identity, hit testing, and URI policy remain neutral.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if ORBF no longer carries one unambiguous target for the presented link.
- Stop if the design requires reparsing text, changing terminal authority, or adding a protocol adapter.
- Stop for user choice if safe platform opening requires a new dependency or materially different Linux/macOS policy.

5. Unsupported schemes, oversized or malformed targets, and native-open failure produce bounded, accessible UX.
6. Deterministic checks cover target identity, geometry invalidation, policy, and failure. Manual Linux dogfood covers hover, copy, open, terminal mouse mode, and keyboard access.

title: Provide structured terminal accessibility
description:
Contract routing:
- Creates VEN-C6 when implementation is explicitly activated.
- Hardens VEN-C1 and VEN-C4 while consuming the exact Orbit presentation proof current at activation.
- Accepted ORB-C8 viewport/history and ORB-C9 selection/copy may enrich VEN-C6 after ven-4sn; a future user-approved semantic-region contract may add landmarks. None blocks a correct visible-viewport slice. Planning this Bead changes no contract index or runtime behavior.

## Why

Venus currently exposes the entire scene as one flattened AccessKit Terminal node. That announces content and failures but does not provide row structure, text ranges, selection, link navigation, or useful actions for screen-reader users.

## Evidence

- `src/accessibility.rs:31-40` creates one Terminal or Alert content node.
- `src/accessibility.rs:76-123` stores one flattened scene value.
- `src/scene.rs:203-214` concatenates the visible grid into accessible text.
- `src/accessibility.rs:169-173` proves only the flattened Terminal value and Alert.
- `docs/CRATES.md:12,65-76` assigns accessibility adaptation to AccessKit and requires it to derive from the accepted immutable scene.

## Scope

In scope:
- A bounded structured accessibility tree derived from the same accepted scene used for drawing.
- Stable visible row/text-run identity, text ranges and selection where AccessKit supports them, explicit link roles/actions, cursor/focus state, and failure/effect alerts.
- Keyboard and assistive-technology actions mapped through existing Venus interaction owners.
- Linux screen-reader dogfood and a macOS-credible tree/update design.

Out of scope:
- A second terminal document model, unbounded scrollback nodes, OCR/pixel inference, a custom accessibility framework, macOS support claims, or waiting for GPU presentation before answering an accessibility activation request.
design:
## Implementation Notes

1. Add user-approved VEN-C6 before code and record the exact consumed Orbit revision.
2. Complete the Execution baseline and Reference gate. Required before code: AccessKit 0.24.1 tree, text, selection, action, focus, and live-region APIs; accesskit_winit 0.33.2 update/activation behavior; current Linux AT-SPI behavior; and one mature native terminal accessibility implementation at an exact revision. Classify later history/semantic sources as conditional.
3. Keep one Scene-derived accessibility projection. Use stable revision/row/run identities and window the tree to visible content plus only a deliberately bounded nearby range.
4. Route accessibility actions through existing Venus semantic input, selection, link, scroll, and copy owners. Never mutate a parallel content model.
5. Publish the latest accepted scene on activation even when rendering is occluded or recovering.
6. Add deterministic tree/action transition checks, then dogfood with at least one Linux screen reader. Compilation and snapshots alone do not prove usability.
7. When ven-4sn accepts ORB-C8 and ORB-C9, extend the same tree with the accepted viewport and selection state. Add prompt/input/output landmarks only after a separately approved Orbit semantic-region contract; do not reserve or assume an ORB-C ID here.

Dependency decision: reuse the accepted AccessKit stack. Any new accessibility crate, toolkit, or platform bridge requires a Crate gate and user approval.

Portability disposition: neutral scene-to-tree core with isolated platform adapters; actual macOS behavior remains unproved.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if required semantics are absent from the Orbit scene rather than inferring them.
- Stop if a proposed tree is unbounded or mirrors the entire terminal independently.
- Stop for user choice if AccessKit cannot express a required contract without another architecture-shaping dependency.
- Stop if deterministic checks pass but real assistive technology exposes a materially different interaction model; record the dogfood gap.
acceptance_criteria:
1. VEN-C6 is approved and indexed before implementation with the exact Orbit contracts and proof revision consumed.
2. The accessibility tree is derived solely from the accepted immutable Scene and cannot advance to unaccepted or stale presentation content.
3. Visible rows and text runs expose stable bounded structure, correct grapheme text, cursor/focus, link identity, selection/ranges where supported, and explicit status/effect alerts.
4. Accessibility activation receives a current tree even while the GPU surface is occluded, lost, or recovering.
5. Actions route through the same Venus interaction owners as pointer and keyboard behavior and never create terminal authority.
6. Tree size and update cost remain bounded under rapid output, resize, reconnect, large viewports, and status churn.
7. Strong deterministic checks cover tree transitions, IDs, Unicode, links, selection, actions, reconnect, occlusion, and failures.
8. Manual Linux screen-reader dogfood records navigation, reading order, focus, link activation, copy/selection, resize, and failure UX. Unsupported platform behavior remains explicit.
9. Locked canonical checks pass and closure records proof revision, dependency disposition, portability, LOC, dogfood environment, and limitations.
notes:
Priority P2: important product quality and a direct architectural advantage of structured presentation, but the existing flattened tree already provides a minimum accessible status/content baseline.

External gate: implement after an Orbit/Venus graduation go and orb-bi4.7 disposition unless the user explicitly activates it earlier. ORB-C8, ORB-C9, and any later approved semantic-region contract are enhancements, not prerequisites for a bounded visible-screen improvement.

Rejected alternatives: one giant unstructured value as the final design, OCR, pixel scraping, exposing a full unbounded scrollback document, coupling accessibility updates to successful GPU presentation, or changing the terminal protocol solely to mirror AccessKit structures.

Planning estimate: effort M; implementation risk MED (assistive-technology behavior and update bounds); confidence MED until real Linux screen-reader dogfood validates the tree.

title: Render one accepted Orbit session in a minimum Linux window
description: Implement the smallest Venus slice: one Linux window consumes canonical structured frames from an already-running Orbit session, renders their accepted rich state, sends semantic input and resize, remains transient across client exit, and explains bounded attachment or server failure.
design:
Begin only after the user activates Venus, accepts the backend and composition decision, and accepts one exact-revision canonical Orbit protocol-consumption shape. Pin the exact accepted Orbit commit and ORB-C1 through ORB-C7 states. Decode accepted ORBF v1 complete frames into one persistent Venus PresentationState before producing draw inputs; reconnect and resync replace that state coherently. This keeps a later user-approved patch protocol compatible with the same reducer model without implementing patches now.

Before manual window dogfood, use a bounded canonical frame corpus or the smallest protocol-faithful source to prove deterministic decode and frame-to-draw inputs without a live PTY, handwritten mirror schema, raw VT parser, or second terminal authority.
